name.description: Optional name locally unique to the parent {@link FlowGraph}. Useful for user-facing APIs such as visualization.

inTypes.description:
key - port name
value - information about type associated with this port. This is useful for {@link FlowGraph.Edge} validation.

outTypes.description:
key - port name
value - information about type associated with this port. This is useful for {@link FlowGraph.Edge} validation.

parents.description:
ids of parent vertices in {@Workflow#parent} {@link FlowGraph}. NOTE: there can be multiple in the case
that several vertices in the parent {@link FlowGraph} were merged as part of translation to a single vertex
in the new graph.

timeout.description:
Timeout for the execution of the vertex. After timeout time has passed the vertex execution fails if not
successfully completed or failed already.

targetType.description:
Inputs will be made into a single object or map of type specified by {@link #targetType}.
See typedoc for examples.

title:
A specialized {@link Workflow.Vertex} that represents an object or map "make" operation.
This is often done to merge several data outputs into a single input for a {@link Workflow.Action}.
All the inputs of this vertex are combined into a single object of type {@link #targetType}
```
-------------------                            ----------------------
| Workflow.Action  | out ----------------> a   |                     |
-------------------                            |                     |                        --------------------
                                               |   Workflow.Make     |  out -------------> in | Workflow.Action |
-------------------                            |                     |                        --------------------
| Workflow.Action  | out ----------------> b   |                     |
-------------------                            ----------------------
```
As an example of the "make" operation, assume the {@link Workflow.Make} instance visually depicted above and that
the values passed to `a` and `b` are "hello" and 42, respectively.
If {@link #targetType} is an {@link Obj}:
```
// targetType = MyObj.myType()
type MyObj {
  a: !string
  b: !int
}
// out = MyObj(a="hello", b=42)
```
If {@link #targetType} is an {@link Map}:
```
// out = {"a": "hello", "b": 42}
```
name: Workflow.Make
